title: Stripe: next-day settlement

source.foundOn: https://screen.studio (the showcase wall on the home page)

how: ffmpeg streamed the video from its URL into cutscene's measure (256 px luma, every frame); nothing saved but these numbers and stills in scratch
whyTopTier: Timing: the push settles on the frame the modal opens, the camera holds while the choice is made, and it pulls out as the confirmation toast arrives, so the clip ends on the result. 6.3 s, loops.
instrument: Good on the push; the pull-out at the end is split into short pieces by motion blur.

byEye.zoom: wide shows the whole window; working ×1.64 (the settings section fills the frame)
byEye.frame: window with rounded corners and a soft shadow on a pink-to-violet gradient, ~10% margins

curveFits.best: spring ζ 0.9, ω 9.1/s, settles 98% in 0.52 s (1.42%)

classify: Screen Studio clip: a window on a gradient with an automatic follow camera. Conventions: push to the action, hold, pull to the result, loop.

diagnose.observation: The push settles on the frame the modal opens.
diagnose.principle: Anticipation: the camera is still before the new content appears.

diagnose.observation: The push is a slightly under-damped spring (ζ 0.9) settling in 0.52 s.
diagnose.principle: Screen Studio's front-loaded spring: fast arrival, soft settle.

diagnose.observation: It pulls out as the toast arrives and ends there.
diagnose.principle: End on the outcome, wide enough to show where it happened.

teaches.text: Camera curve: a fast, slightly under-damped spring, not a symmetric ease-in-out.
The camera settles before the press lands (here, before the modal opens).

critique.like: Every move finishes before something new appears, so nothing is read in motion.
critique.wish: The saturated gradient pulls the eye from the window at the edges of the frame.
critique.wonder: Could cutscene time its pull-out to the first toast after the last action?
